script.title: They Posted Hidden Codes Worldwide to Recruit Geniuses
sentences: In 2012, an anonymous user launched a global recruitment test online.
The initial puzzle appeared on 4chan, hiding data inside digital images.
Soon, physical paper signs bearing QR codes turned up in public places.
People claimed the NSA, CIA, MI6, or Mossad were secretly hiring codebreakers.
Solvers who passed gained access to a private forum.
A third round of puzzles launched on Twitter in 2014.
That third puzzle remains completely unsolved.
The group posted its last verified message in 2017 and went silent.
script.description: Cicada 3301 released complex cryptographic challenges across the globe to recruit master codebreakers. Their final puzzle has never been solved.
visuals: QR code paper poster street pole
claims_en: In 2012, an anonymous entity posted an online puzzle to recruit intelligent individuals.
The first puzzle was posted on 4chan and concealed data within digital images using steganography.
The puzzles incorporated physical clues like paper signs with QR codes.
Speculation arose that intelligence agencies like the NSA, CIA, MI6, or Mossad were behind the recruiting.
Successful solvers were invited to a private forum.
A third round of puzzles was posted on Twitter in 2014.
Cicada 3301 posted their last verified OpenPGP-signed message in April 2017.
